newsitem.title: ITALY: Centre-left candidate leads in Ancona - Italy poll.
newsitem.headline: Centre-left candidate leads in Ancona - Italy poll.

text.p: Italy's governing centre-left coalition led in a mayoral race in Ancona on the Adriatic coast, according to a forecast based on more than three-quarters of votes cast in Sunday's municipal elections.
Renato Galeazzi, the Olive Tree coalition's candidate, was in front with 44.6 percent of the vote after a first round of voting, a forecast released by the Abacus polling institute said on Monday.
Loris Mancinelli of the centre-right opposition Freedom Alliance was in second place with 36.1 percent, followed by the Communist Refoundation's Lidia Mangani who polled 12.6 percent of the vote.

Abacus said the Olive Tree were also ahead in the north-eastern town of Pordenone with Claudio Cudin expected to get 34.8 percent, slightly ahead of the separatist Northern League and centre-right candidates.
With almost all the votes counted in the Tuscan town of Grosseto, the Freedom Alliance was set to win 51.3 percent.
A run-off will be held on May 11 between the two leading contenders for mayor in places where no candidate obtains an absolute majority.

The centre-right was ahead in Milan and Turin -- the key contests in elections for mayors and local councils in more than 1,100 towns and cities in the first big test of electoral support since Prime Minister Romano Prodi's coalition won last April's general election. -- Rome newsroom +396-6782501
